newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end down, brisk speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end down, brisk speculative selling.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled sharply weaker in technically-driven speculative selling, market sources said.
July closed 1.55 cents lower at 74.55 cents per lb, traded 76.10 to 74.25 cents. September ended down 1.65 at 76.90 cents, while the outer months settled 1.40 to 0.55 lower.
Early selling triggered stops and sent second-position September to a life-of-contract low of 76.55 cents.
November also hit a contract low of 79.75 cents.
July managed to hold above its downside target of 74.00 cents ahead of today's options expiry, as open interest in July 75.00-cent calls and puts, remains high.
Open interest in the July futures contract also remains high at 14,671 lots, ahead of the first notice day on July 1.

Some of the smaller speculators thought to be holdiing the majority of contracts. The last NYCE spec/hedge report released on Tuesday showed the speculators to be holding a 65.4 percent long position, and a 21.3 percent short position.

"If (the speculators) choose to exit the market rather than carry their trades forward, the market could be vulnerable to a drop through recent support levels," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes, said in a weekly citrus comment.
Nearby support in July was seen at 74.00 cents, followed by 72.30 cents and then 70.35 cents.
An estimated 4,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 3,501 lots.

There has been no change in the bearish fundamental situation during the past week. With the 1996/97 harvest nearly complete, Florida is expected to produce a record 224.2 million 90-lb boxes, the U.S. Department of Agriculture, said.
The media continues to put forth stories about Medfly infestation to the Florida crop, but agriculture officials expect damage to be light.
